book_vs_repo_gap: This appendix captures taxonomy and simple WSD in miniature, but omits large lexical resources, supervised WSD, and richer semantic relations.

chapter_notes.counterintuitive_insight: Word-sense resources are most useful when they fail: taxonomy and context are different signals, and forcing them together reveals the real problem.
covered_claims: This appendix separates lexical hierarchy from context-sensitive disambiguation.
A toy WordNet graph and gloss-overlap WSD are both explicit.
omitted_claims: No full synset inventory or relation types beyond tiny samples.

failure_modes.note: Changing context wording can flip WSD even when meaning stays constant.
WordNet graph distance captures ontology structure, not contextual usage.

lesson_objectives: Represent lexical hierarchy as a graph.
Contrast taxonomy-based similarity with context-based WSD.

reference_experiments.expected_signal: taxonomic closeness differs from contextual ambiguity
reference_experiments.name: hierarchy_vs_context
